name: nest
note: Large real OSS target (~1676 walked TS files: packages 830 + integration 501 + sample 329 — realistic monorepo noise). Ground truth verified by exploration at the pinned commit, 2026-07-22.

questions.question: Which files implement NestJS's dependency injection: the container, the module scanning, and the actual provider instantiation? Name the exact files and their roles.
questions.criteria: Names packages/core/injector/container.ts (NestContainer registry), packages/core/scanner.ts (DependenciesScanner — recursive module walk before instantiation), packages/core/injector/injector.ts (Injector — resolveConstructorParams/instantiateClass), and packages/core/injector/instance-loader.ts (InstanceLoader driving instantiation per module). Bonus: module.ts or instance-wrapper.ts with correct roles.

questions.question: Trace a request through NestJS's enhancer pipeline: in what order do guards, interceptors, pipes, and exception filters run, and which file orchestrates that order?
questions.criteria: Names packages/core/router/router-execution-context.ts (RouterExecutionContext.create) as the orchestrator and gives the verified order: guards first, interceptors wrapping the call, pipes running immediately before the controller method inside the interceptor-wrapped handler, exception filters wrapping one level up via router-proxy.ts / exceptions-handler.ts. An answer with the wrong order (e.g. pipes before guards) caps at 5.

questions.question: Where do @Controller, @Injectable, and the HTTP method decorators like @Get live, and where are the metadata keys they write defined?
questions.criteria: Names packages/common/decorators/core/controller.decorator.ts, packages/common/decorators/core/injectable.decorator.ts, packages/common/decorators/http/request-mapping.decorator.ts (RequestMapping, exporting Get/Post/...), and packages/common/constants.ts as the metadata-constants file (PATH_METADATA, METHOD_METADATA, watermarks).

questions.question: I want to contribute a new microservices transport to this repo (say, for ZeroMQ). Which directories and files do I create or touch, and what existing code should I use as a template?
questions.criteria: Identifies both halves: a server implementation in packages/microservices/server/ (new server-zeromq.ts extending Server from server.ts) registered in server-factory.ts, and a client proxy in packages/microservices/client/ (extending ClientProxy from client-proxy.ts) registered in client-proxy-factory.ts. ANY existing transport pair (mqtt, redis, nats, rmq, tcp) is an equally valid template — do not penalize the choice. Bonus: names the concrete methods to implement (listen/close/bindEvents; connect/publish/dispatchEvent).

questions.question: What would be affected if I changed the NestContainer / Injector internals in packages/core/injector — which parts of the codebase are the tightest couplings?
questions.criteria: Identifies nest-factory.ts (bootstrap constructs both), instance-loader.ts, module-ref.ts (runtime bridge), the router resolution pair (routes-resolver.ts / router-explorer.ts consuming controller instances), and instance-wrapper.ts as the most-imported injector primitive. Bonus: cross-package couplings — packages/microservices (microservices-module, listeners-controller) and packages/websockets/socket-module.ts import NestContainer directly. Conveys scale (dozens of importers), not just one file.

questions.question: How does the NestJS REPL work under the hood — what does it start, and how does it get access to the application's providers?
questions.criteria: Explains that repl() (packages/core/repl/repl.ts) starts no server — it creates a headless application context via NestFactory.createApplicationContext, then ReplContext (packages/core/repl/repl-context.ts) reaches into the app's private container field and walks container.getModules() to introspect providers/controllers. Bonus: native commands registered via repl-native-commands.ts / native-functions/.
